assertionResults.reason: A mixed-status run produced all five states simultaneously: standard=healthy, fast=degraded (3.014s), longctx=down (timeout), idle=crashed (dead PID), litellm=stopped.

Status used per-service health checks with timeout behavior: first service down timed out (response_time null) while subsequent fast/longctx/litellm checks still completed healthy; total runtime was ~5.147s for the timed-out-first run.

Default status output rendered a formatted table with Tier/Model/Port/Status/Uptime columns; running tiers displayed human-readable uptime (e.g., 2m 5s), while crashed/stopped tiers showed "-" uptime.
`status --json` was valid parseable JSON containing tier/model/port/status/uptime fields for each service, and statuses/ports matched table output for the same run.
With no stack file, status returned the expected "No stack configured" guidance in table and JSON modes; with stack present and no PID files, all services reported stopped with no traceback.
After externally killing the fast-tier process, status reported that tier as crashed (not stopped/healthy) with dash uptime.
Read-only verification showed zero changes to tracked stack/config/pid/lock files across a status run; status also succeeded while a delayed up command was holding lifecycle lock state (concurrency).
Lifecycle stage status transitions matched contract: before up all stopped, after up all healthy, after down all stopped, and after external kill the killed tier reported crashed.

frictions.description: Initial init invocation failed because PATH omitted /usr/sbin, so sysctl lookup failed during hardware detection.
frictions.resolution: Re-ran commands with system path entries (/usr/sbin:/sbin) included in PATH.

frictions.description: Python http.server-based shim responders were non-responsive in this environment for health checks, causing false down states.
frictions.resolution: Replaced isolation-only shim implementations with socket-based HTTP responders and re-ran all affected status lifecycle checks.

summary: Tested 8 assigned assertions via real CLI surface in isolated MLX_STACK_HOME. All 8 assertions passed with evidence for no-stack handling, five-state classification, JSON/table consistency, timeout continuation behavior, read-only status semantics, and cross-stage lifecycle transitions.
